steps.intro: Twenty years after university, Rachel walks through a farmers' market in Yorkshire — and the man at the cheese stall looks very familiar. Part 1: fill the gaps. The glossary is beside the text.

p: Sorry — Tom? Tom Hale?
…Rachel? Rachel Price? No way!
! It must be… twenty years?
At least. Last time I saw you, we were both in black gowns, throwing hats in the air.
Don't remind me — I nearly lost an eye. So… what are you doing behind a cheese stall?
It's my cheese stall. I make cheese now.
You make cheese?!
, you were at that huge law firm in London!
I was. I was a lawyer for fifteen years. Then I left.
But you were the most serious person in our year! You wore a tie to lectures!
Only on Mondays.
So how did you
cheese, of all things?
It's a bit of a long story. Have you got ten minutes?
For this? I've got all day.
OK. You remember I never really wanted to do law?
Vaguely. Didn't you want to be a vet?
I did. But I didn't get into vet school, and my mum said I'd make a great lawyer because I argued with everyone. So I
law instead. That's just what everyone did back then, wasn't it? Then I
a solicitor, worked crazy hours for fifteen years… and one day I just couldn't do it any more.
So what happened?
Completely
, I saw an ad for a weekend course in cheesemaking. I signed up for a laugh — and I loved it. Then a place came up on a six-month course, so I took a break from work, and eventually a job
on a farm up here. I never went back.
Long time no see!
